**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE), confidence 0.82.**

What I checked:
- Full-text search for "insurance" — only incidental hits in Article I definitions (freight/insurance costs in the Net Sales deduction; "health insurance ... payers' charges"). No covenant.
- Article XVI (Indemnification; Recalls, p0715–p0727 plus 16.6 Recalls) — indemnities and a consequential-damages disclaimer, but no insurance backstop.
- Article XVIII (General Provisions, p0759–p0796) — runs 18.1 through 18.14 with no insurance section.

Direction: Array is the licensor but also manufactures/supplies Product and sponsors Clinical Studies, and gives Ono product-liability and recall indemnities under Section 16.2. An insurance covenant therefore supports our position; I drafted it as a one-way obligation on Array so it does not add any reciprocal burden on Ono (whose own indemnity under 16.1 is broad).

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new **Section 18.15 Insurance** inserted after 18.14, at the preferred limits — CGL USD 1M/2M (expanded to include products and clinical trial liability, appropriate for a pharma licence), E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M conditioned on Array handling our personal data/Confidential Information, workers' comp per law, certificates on request. The comment offers the fallback (E&O 1M / cyber 2M) as a landing zone.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the parties are to execute separate Supply and Quality Agreements (Section 18.7), which may already carry manufacturing insurance — limits can be aligned there instead of duplicated.
